record.context_brief: Omega theorem for shifted divisor sums
record.original_question: For k >= 3, let D_{k,2}(x, h) = sum_{n<=x} d_k(n) d_2(n+h), and let M_{k,2}(x, h) denote the main term in the known asymptotic formula. Prove an omega theorem for the error D_{k,2}(x, h) - M_{k,2}(x, h).

evidence.quote: Topacogullari [68], [70] and Drappeau [33] have proven asymptotic formulae for Dk,2(x, h). Prove an omega theorem for Dk,2(x, h)−Mk,2 (x, h) for k >= 3 where Mk,2 (x, h) is the main term in the asymptotic formula.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $k\ge 2$, let $d_k(n)$ denote the $k$-fold divisor function, i.e. the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into $k$ positive integer factors (so $d_2(n)$ is the usual divisor function). For a fixed nonzero integer $h$ and a real $x\ge 2$, define the shifted convolution sum
$$D_{k,2}(x,h)\;=\;\sum_{n\le x} d_k(n)\,d_2(n+h).$$
It is known that for every $k\ge 3$ there exists an asymptotic formula
$$D_{k,2}(x,h)\;=\;M_{k,2}(x,h)\;+\;E_{k,2}(x,h),$$
where the main term $M_{k,2}(x,h)$ is a polynomial in $\log x$ of degree $k$ (with coefficients depending on $h$) and $E_{k,2}(x,h)=o(x\,(\log x)^k)$ as $x\to\infty$.

Establish an omega-type lower bound for the error term $E_{k,2}(x,h)=D_{k,2}(x,h)-M_{k,2}(x,h)$ valid for every $k\ge 3$. Concretely, prove the existence of an explicit function $f_k(x)\to\infty$ (depending on $k$) such that
$$E_{k,2}(x,h)\;=\;\Omega\!\bigl(f_k(x)\bigr)$$
as $x\to\infty$, i.e. $\limsup_{x\to\infty}|E_{k,2}(x,h)|/f_k(x)>0$.
artifact.status_search_result: Asymptotic formulas with power-saving error terms for D_{k,2}(x,h) are known for k≥3 due to Topacogullari and Drappeau, but the available literature establishes only upper bounds on the error term. No omega-type lower bound for D_{k,2}(x,h)−M_{k,2}(x,h) for general k≥3 appears in the search results, so the problem appears to remain open. Omega results are known in related but distinct settings (e.g. the classical divisor problem and twisted divisor functions).

status_evidence.title: The shifted convolution of generalized divisor functions
status_evidence.snippet: Topacogullari proved asymptotic formulae for shifted convolutions of d_k and d with power-saving error terms for k≥3.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic formulas for D_{k,2}(x,h) are established, but only upper bounds on the error are given.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial identities and Titchmarsh's divisor problem for multiplicative functions
status_evidence.snippet: Drappeau obtains asymptotic expansions for shifted convolution sums of multiplicative functions with power-saving error terms.
status_evidence.claim: Drappeau's work provides the main term M_{k,2}(x,h) and upper bounds on E_{k,2}, not omega lower bounds.

status_evidence.title: Omega Theorems for The Twisted Divisor Function
status_evidence.snippet: Omega results for twisted divisor functions are obtained, but no analogous result for shifted convolutions D_{k,2} is given.
status_evidence.claim: Omega bounds exist for related divisor problems, suggesting the shifted-convolution analogue remains open.
